title: Prioritized alert sampling and automated surge cookbooks for multi-region SLO degradations
creator: Priya Menon
description: Problem: During regional load spikes we see a flood of low-signal alerts (cached miss spikes, transient backend 503s) that drown on-call attention and cause noisy escalations. Root causes cross multiple layers: overaggressive alert thresholds, lack of per-route de-duplication, brittle circuit-breaker hysteresis, and no automated play for graceful load-shedding. Goal: implement a lightweight, intent-aware alert sampling layer plus an automated surge "cookbook" that sequences graded mitigations (sampling, soft-shutdown, circuit hysteresis tuning, and traffic shed) with on-call guidance and automated runbook execution where safe.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route alert sampling implemented and configurable per-SLO tier (revocable config) with sampling factors persisted in config-store

Automated surge cookbook steps implemented as composable runbook actions (notify-only, sample X%, mute X min, increase circuit hysteresis, trigger load-shed policy) invoked via webhook or platform API
Runbook actions have playbacks (dry-run) safe mode and a clearly documented rollback path
Reduction of pager volume for known transient events by >= 60% in canary region during simulated spike
No escalations lost: all sampled/muted alerts are stored and surfaced in a post-incident summary dashboard
End-to-end test harness and chaos scenarios added to CI (synthetic KV cache storm, backend 503 burst, cross-region latency spike).
tasks: Audit top-25 alert rules by signal/noise ratio and tag candidates for sampling
Design sampling policy schema (priority, sample_rate, window, reason-code) and publish to config-store
Implement gateway middleware that enforces sampling + enriches suppressed alerts with context and retention tag
Build runbook action primitives as idempotent API endpoints (notify, sample, mute, modify-hysteresis, trigger-shed, escalate)
Author surge cookbook (graded steps) for SLO degradation types: prefix-KV-cache-miss, downstream-503, high-rt-p90
Add CI chaos tests and telemetry assertions to verify behavior under synthetic events
Console: dashboard tile for sampled alerts, actionable links to runbook play execution, and post-incident summary generator
Prepare rollout plan: canary in eu-west-1, monitor 2 weeks, then staged global rollout

timeline: Jan 15: design kickoff -> Jan 22: middleware prototype -> Jan 25: persistence decision -> Feb 02: action primitives -> Feb 09: console mockups and security review -> Feb 16: canary rollout in eu-west-1 (planned)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-suppression hides an emerging incident. Mitigation: Persist suppressed alerts and require an automatic replay if suppressed-delta rate > threshold
Risk: Runbook action APIs could be abused. Mitigation: mTLS + HMAC + action RBAC and audit logs; rate-limit modifications to hysteresis parameters
Risk: Interaction with circuit-breakers may cause oscillation. Mitigation: add minimum hysteresis window and backoff multiplier; validate with CI chaos tests
testing_plan: Unit tests for sampling logic and deterministic hashing
Integration tests that verify persistence of suppressed alerts and replay plumbing
Chaos tests: KV cache miss storm, downstream-503 burst, cross-region latency spike
Canary validation: synthetic incidents injected in eu-west-1, measure pager volume, time-to-detect, and false-negative rate
notes: This ticket focuses on the orchestration layer (sampling + runbook actions). Separate follow-ups will tune specific circuit-breaker kernels and implement advanced load-shed strategies in the runtime (tracked in a follow-up ENG ticket).
postmortem_plan: If canary shows >15% increase in missed critical alerts or any escalation delays >5 minutes, automatically roll back sampling for that route and open an incident review. Postmortem will include: timeline, suppressed alert replay, decision log, telemetry graphs, and remediation plan.
